text:
jdoe_customer: Hey team, after we moved the internal API to the new infra account, our service endpoint service.internal.myapp keeps intermittently NXDOMAINing from our app instances. Started ~0200 UTC. No changes to app code. Can you help?

maria_support: Sorry you're seeing that — can you paste a dig output from one of the failing instances? Also which VPC (id) and region?

jdoe_customer: VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d in us-east-1. Here's a quick dig from an app host: 
```
$ dig +short service.internal.myapp @172.31.0.2
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached

$ dig service.internal.myapp @172.31.0.2
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
```

samir_ops: connection timed out to .2 is odd. Is that the VPC provided resolver? Check /etc/resolv.conf on the instance and paste it.

jdoe_customer: resolv.conf shows: 
```
nameserver 172.31.0.2
search ip-172-31-0-ec2.internal
options timeout:2 attempts:2
```

aaron_sre: Can you run `dig +trace service.internal.myapp` (no @) so we can see where it fails in lookup chain? Also run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones` for the account where the new infra was created and in the app account (if you have access).

jdoe_customer: Trace shows it hits VPC resolver then NXDOMAIN. I don't have cross-account list rights — ticketed ops to check.

julie_eng: Quick checklist we do for split-horizon/Route53 private DNS issues: 
- check for multiple private hosted zones with the same zone name associated with the same VPC (this causes ambiguous/undefined resolution)
- check resolver rule associations and conditional forwarders
- check VPC association count on each private hosted zone
- check for any Route53 resolver endpoints that could be forwarding to on-prem
- clear instance DNS caches (nscd/dnsmasq) after changes

maria_support: Also verify there are no leftover security group/iptables rules blocking UDP/53 to 172.31.0.2 (rare but we've seen it).

DNS-bot: automated check results for vpc-0a1b2c3d (from our central tooling): 
```
- Found private hosted zone "internal.myapp" in account-APP (hz-aaaa) associated with vpc-0a1b2c3d
- Found private hosted zone "internal.myapp" in account-INFRA (hz-bbbb) ALSO associated with vpc-0a1b2c3d
- Resolver rules: none
- No resolver endpoints
```

samir_ops: Bingo — two private hosted zones with identical names both associated with the same VPC. AWS behavior is undocumented/ambiguous in this case, which can produce NXDOMAIN or records from either zone unpredictably.

jdoe_customer: How did that happen? We only intended the infra team to own the zone.

aaron_sre: Looks like the legacy app account had an older private zone (hz-aaaa). When infra created the new zone in the infra account and associated it during migration, both associations remained. AWS allows multiple private hosted zones with same name to be associated to the same VPC across accounts — results are undefined.

julie_eng: Fix path: disassociate the legacy zone (hz-aaaa) from the VPC, keep the new infra zone (hz-bbbb) associated. Steps we used: 
1) Confirm which hosted zone actually has the expected records via `aws route53 list-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id hz-xxxx`
2) From account-APP: `aws route53 disassociate-vpc --hosted-zone-id hz-aaaa --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d`
3) Wait a minute, restart nscd on a couple of app hosts: `sudo systemctl restart nscd` (or `sudo service nscd restart`)
4) Verify `dig +short service.internal.myapp @172.31.0.2` returns the expected A/ALIAS

maria_support: We can do the disassociate for you if you approve and provide the hosted zone id to remove.

jdoe_customer: Please go ahead, disassociate hz-aaaa. I'll monitor and confirm.

(15 minutes later)

dns-bot: action log: route53 disassociate-vpc called on hz-aaaa from vpc-0a1b2c3d by maria_support at 1793457965

aaron_sre: After disassociate, on one of the app instances: 
```
$ dig +short service.internal.myapp @172.31.0.2
10.1.4.22
```

jdoe_customer: Confirmed — resolving now and no NXDOMAINs. Thanks.

samir_ops: Follow-ups: 
- Create a small detection alert in our infra audit (dns-bot) for duplicated private hosted zones associated with the same VPC across accounts — we'll add severity medium.
- Add a note to migration runbook: verify old hosted zones are fully disassociated before associating new ones.

maria_support: Also opened support ticket with customer to document steps taken and asked app team to restart DNS caches across all instances.

jdoe_customer: Appreciated. One more Q: will deleting the old hosted zone be safe? It's currently unused but owned by the app account.

julie_eng: Deleting is safe once disassociated and after you confirm no other VPCs rely on it. Recommend: disassociate -> verify for 72 hours -> then delete if no issues. We'll help validate cross-VPC associations before deletion.

maria_support: Closing this thread once customer confirms post-72hr. :white_check_mark:

(End of thread)
